applies_why: The judge text makes an UNDERDETERMINED ruling on a link and states the grounds for it, so K-S2 governs the ruling.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: Phrase: single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. Two readings weighed: it forbids only a bare one-verse silence ground, or it broadly forbids any UNDERDETERMINED involving a verse not stating the link; I used the first because the judge cites comparative chains.
why: The judge grounds UNDERDETERMINED on the two chains not forcing each other, not on a single verse's failure to state the link, so K-S2 is not breached.
